task.title: execution:validate and the dry-run execution path have an unpinned cross-module authorization complement
task.objective: execution:runWorkflow authorizes only when request.dryRun === false, and ExecutionApplicationService.runWorkflow short-circuits to { status: "validated" } when request.dryRun !== false. Those two literal predicates in two different modules are exact complements, which is the only reason the ungated path launches no browser - and nothing in the repository asserts that relationship. Flipping the service predicate to === true would create a genuine privilege escalation with every current control still green. KNOWN_ISSUES records the remedy as a decision, not a patch: either document the view-level exemption and add a control pinning it, or gate the paths. Take the documented option, record it as a decision, and pin the complement with a non-vacuous characterization control.

architecture: This task pins an existing invariant; it does not change one. The runtime edit is comment-only at both sites. No predicate, no control flow, no handler registration, and no exported signature may change.

The invariant has two halves in two modules and must be documented at BOTH sites. Commenting only app/main/ipc/execution.ipc.ts would leave the half that actually enforces the no-browser property - ExecutionApplicationService.runWorkflow's dryRun !== false short-circuit - unmarked, which is the exact failure mode this task exists to close.

The pinning control belongs in scripts/verify-r0-characterization.mts, which already source()s both files inside runPreparationCharacterization(). Do not create a new verifier script; that would add a scripts/lib/verifier-classification.ts registry entry and a new npm script for no gain.
Do not edit src/runner/ExecutionEngine.ts, applyRunGateEnforcement, or any sibling IPC handler.
security: Remedy (a) - document the view-level exemption and add a control pinning it - is chosen over remedy (b) - gate the paths - because (b) is a behavior change that breaks a documented product behavior: execution.ipc.ts states that validation/dry-run stays open at view level so a Viewer's pre-run preview works, and no browser is launched on that path. The choice is recorded in docs/ai/DECISIONS.md rather than made silently.

The security property being pinned is a COMPLEMENT relationship, not the presence of a token: the IPC guard runs when request.dryRun === false and the service returns early when request.dryRun !== false. The control must assert both literal predicates, in their own scopes, so that changing either one alone turns the suite red.

The control must additionally assert that the service short-circuit precedes applyRunGateEnforcement and executionEngine.startRun, since the no-browser property depends on that ordering and not only on the predicate.
The control must assert that execution:validate contains exactly zero assertSender* calls. That is the current, deliberate state; asserting it makes any future silent gating or ungating visible.
Cardinality before ordering: every ordering assertion must be preceded by a count assertion on the same collection, so no assertion can pass over an empty set.
Do not weaken, reorder or delete any existing assertion in execution.ipc.ts, ExecutionApplicationService.ts or scripts/verify-r0-characterization.mts.
compatibility: No runtime behavior change of any kind. No IPC signature change, no persisted shape change, no migration. execution:runWorkflow, execution:validate and ExecutionApplicationService.runWorkflow keep their exact parameters, results and semantics.
A Viewer's dry-run pre-run preview must keep working exactly as before; that is precisely the behavior remedy (b) would have broken.
offline: No network access, no new dependency, no packaging change, no new npm script.

acceptance.description: docs/ai/DECISIONS.md records the view-level dry-run exemption as a deliberate decision with its reasoning - that gating would break the documented Viewer pre-run preview and that no browser is launched on the ungated path - and names the control that pins it. The docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md awkit-ttvb entry moves from open finding with an undecided remedy to resolved, citing the recorded decision. The KNOWN_ISSUES instruction 'do not silently pick one' is satisfied by an explicit written record, not by an unstated preference.

Comments at BOTH halves of the invariant name it and name the control: app/main/ipc/execution.ipc.ts at the execution:runWorkflow dryRun guard, and app/main/execution/ExecutionApplicationService.ts at the runWorkflow dryRun short-circuit. Each states that the two predicates are complements and that changing one alone is a security change. Both edits are comment-only.

A control in scripts/verify-r0-characterization.mts asserts, scoped by ipcHandlerSpan, that the execution:runWorkflow authorization guard is conditioned on exactly the predicate request.dryRun === false, and that the execution:validate handler contains exactly zero assertSender* calls. Both assertions state a cardinality before any ordering or identity expression.

The same control asserts, scoped by methodBodySpan to ExecutionApplicationService.runWorkflow, that the short-circuit predicate is exactly request.dryRun !== false, and that the short-circuit return precedes both applyRunGateEnforcement and executionEngine.startRun. Together with the guard assertion this pins the complement relationship across the two modules, which is the property nothing previously asserted.

Every assertion block that is INDEPENDENTLY LOAD-BEARING is proven to REJECT a broken source shape through the file's own mutateOnce/mutationRejected mechanism, and each mutant trips a distinct assertion first, verified against the observed failure line rather than predicted. The single exception is stated rather than papered over: assertion block (5), the complement relation itself, is logically ENTAILED by blocks (2)+(3), so no mutant can fail on (5) alone - the escalation mutant A is rejected by (3)'s structural operator check before (5) is reached. Block (5) is therefore defense-in-depth against a future refactor that relaxes (2) or (3), and is NOT independently proven. No assertion was weakened to manufacture a mutant for it, which would have been the dishonest way to make this criterion read cleanly. At minimum: flipping the service predicate to === true (the escalation this task exists to prevent), flipping the IPC guard to !== false, adding an assertSender call to execution:validate, and moving the short-circuit after applyRunGateEnforcement. A TypeScript compile error is never accepted as mutation evidence - only the control's own rejection is. Source is restored exactly after each mutation.

The runtime diff is comment-only and provably changes no behavior: npm run build typechecks clean, and npm run verify:security still reports 61 passed / 0 failed, matching the historical pin, so the authorization surface is byte-equivalent in effect.

The implementation diff touches app/main/ipc/execution.ipc.ts, app/main/execution/ExecutionApplicationService.ts and scripts/verify-r0-characterization.mts only. src/runner/ExecutionEngine.ts is unmodified, no sibling IPC handler is altered, no new verifier script is created, and the separately tracked awkit-9a1l, awkit-utbf, awkit-s410, awkit-wknd and awkit-dhw6 are left alone. Completed awkit-syaa is not reopened.

The evidence item is defined as an applicability DETERMINATION: PASS attests that the determination was executed and returned a definitive answer, and does not assert that mock-site coverage of this boundary exists.
